findings.title: THE QUEUED CALLER'S FAILURE IS PINNED AS A TYPE AND NEVER AS A MESSAGE, so `terminalFailure()` can tell a caller queued behind a DEAD committer that somebody closed the sequencer -- the exact defect round 6 called a major on the sibling path -- with the whole tree green.
findings.surviving_mutation: Replace the whole body of BatchingSequencer.terminalFailure() (BatchingSequencer.java:272-278) with `return new IOException("this sequencer is closed");`, dropping both the abnormal-death wording and the `why` cause chain.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED SURVIVING MUTATION in a copy of the staged tree: `./gradlew test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL, whole tree, with terminalFailure() reduced to a constant close message. Two tests reach that method and neither constrains it: `aQUEUEDCallerIsFailedWithoutWaitingForTheLeaseReleaseToFinish` asserts only `isInstanceOf(IOException.class)`, and `BatchingSequencerLifecycleTest.aCallerQUEUEDBehindADyingCommitterIsFailedEvenWithNoCloseAtAll` (line 207) asserts only `outcomes.hasSize(2)`. The ARRIVING-caller path is pinned by aCommitterThatDIEDDoesNotTELLTheNextCallerItWasCLOSED, but submit() builds its message inline (BatchingSequencer.java:176-181) and never calls terminalFailure(), so that test does not cover it. In production a pod whose committer died with an OutOfMemoryError tells every caller that was QUEUED behind it 'this sequencer is closed', with no cause attached -- an operator debugging a total stall is pointed at a shutdown that never happened, which is verbatim the harm the `terminated` field's own javadoc (BatchingSequencer.java:70-75) claims to prevent. Remedy is one line in either test: `.hasMessageContaining("terminated")` plus a root-cause assertion.
findings.remedy: Add a message/cause assertion to the queued-caller failure in either test; the production code is correct today, only unconstrained.

findings.title: THE `catch (Exception)` -> `catch (Throwable)` WIDENING MADE THIS ROUND IS UNCONSTRAINED: no fixture has a delegate `close()` that throws an Error, so the widening can be reverted with the whole tree green.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED SURVIVING MUTATION in a copy of the staged tree: `./gradlew test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL across every module with the catch narrowed back. Every delegate close in the suite either does nothing, sets a flag, or throws IOException; none throws an Error. In production a store SDK raising a LinkageError or an OutOfMemoryError from `leases.release()` would then escape drainForever's `finally`, so the actionable ERROR log ('releasing the lease after the commit batcher terminated failed; it will now survive to its TTL') never fires and the operator gets an uncaught-exception stack trace from a virtual thread instead. Bounded harm -- the reordering this round means the queue is already failed by then -- which is why this is minor rather than major. A one-line fixture (a delegate whose close throws `new OutOfMemoryError("release")`, asserting the committer's exit still completes) would pin it.
findings.remedy: Either add that fixture or record the widening as untested in the commit body.
